title: Commonwealth of Nations
capsule: The Commonwealth of Nations is a voluntary intergovernmental organisation comprising 56 member states, the majority of them former territories of the British Empire, which formally adopted its current name and structure at the 1949 London Declaration that allowed republics to join while accepting the British monarch as Head of the Commonwealth. It holds biennial Commonwealth Heads of Government Meetings (CHOGM) to coordinate on trade, democracy, and development, but lacks enforcement powers. Membership has expanded beyond strictly former British territories — Rwanda and Mozambique joined despite no historical British connection — while Zimbabwe was suspended in 2002 and withdrew in 2003. The organisation's contemporary relevance is primarily diplomatic, cultural, and through shared legal and sporting traditions including the Commonwealth Games.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Commonwealth is not a territorial polity; mapping it requires the aggregate of member-state polygons, which are individually well-defined but the 'territory' of the organisation is a legal and political construct, not a sovereign boundary.
